asr-publication-v2.description: The complete benchmark set published for transcription models. v2: accuracy on L40S; batch_size is the recommended setting for new runs, and a cell is satisfied at any batch size (the row records the one used). A target may declare max_model_gib: weak reference machines (a base M4, a Ryzen 4750U host) are then required to run only models whose reference publication footprint fits, and larger models are published on the strong reference alone.

single_language_samples.reason: A variant that supports exactly one non-English language is benched on that language at the same two clip lengths as jfk/dots. English jfk/dots decode out of distribution on a single-language fine-tune and can loop until the position cap, and whether that happens differs between CPU and GPU, so the figure would not be comparable.

langid-publication-v1.description: The benchmark set published for language ID (LANGID role) models. Accuracy: open-set top-1 over every label, the macro mean over the FLEURS test languages of scripts/langid/ingest.py, on the first crop_s seconds of each clip without silence trimming, C++ on CPU, every shipped quant; scored by scripts/langid/score.py from one scripts/langid/run.py sweep (all crops), which it also compares against the reference sweep (--ref) for the row's agreement. Speed: scripts/langid/bench.py through the Python binding; a sample <clip>-<N>s is the first N seconds of samples/<clip>.wav.

vad-publication-v1.description: VAD speed only, no accuracy suite (numerical parity is the porting gate). scripts/vad/bench.py through the Python binding, CPU, one thread, every shipped quant. <clip>: transcribe_vad_run over the whole clip. <clip>-<N>ms: one pass of transcribe_vad_stream_feed over the clip in N ms chunks; a cell is the mean time per feed call.

turn-publication-v1.description: The benchmark set published for end-of-turn (TURN role) models. Accuracy: Pipecat's test set pipecat-ai/smart-turn-data-v3.2-test (all 31,527 clips, 23 languages) scored by scripts/turn/eval_cpp.py (tools/transcribe-turn-eval, C++ on CPU, every shipped quant) and scripts/turn/score.py: a clip's score is transcribe_turn_run's p over the whole clip, and a clip is called complete when p > threshold (Pipecat's and Inworld's benchmark rule; not the API's default cut-off). The row's acc_pct is the accuracy at that threshold with a bootstrap 95% interval; its turn object adds the false positives and false negatives as shares of all clips (the convention of Pipecat's published figures, so acc_pct + fp_pct + fn_pct = 100), the count of complete clips and the ROC AUC. Speed: scripts/turn/bench.py through the Python binding's raw C ABI, CPU. <clip>-8s: transcribe_turn_run on the first 8 s of samples/<clip>.wav (Smart Turn's whole window). Streaming models only: <clip>-40ms is one pass of transcribe_turn_stream_feed over the clip in 640-sample (40 ms) feeds, a cell being the mean time per feed; <clip>-40ms-x8 is one pass of transcribe_turn_stream_feed_batch over 8 sessions each fed the clip, a cell being the mean time per tick (one 40 ms frame for each of the 8 users, so sample_duration_s is 0.32 s of audio). A -1t suffix runs the cell on one thread; without it, the library's default thread count (n_threads 0).

targets.display: Apple M1 (proxy for the Apple M4 reference machine, which was unreachable)
